hints: Take the tangent of both sides: $4x = \tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\sqrt{3}$, and solve for $x$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the exact inverse cosine term on the right-hand side:
$$\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6} \implies -\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{6}$$

Apply the tangent function to both sides:
$$4x = \tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\sqrt{3}$$

Solve for $x$ in exact surd form:
$$x = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$$
